A generator that exhausted its declared box, audited every reject, and produced no REFUSED and no schema-invalid candidate earned the certificate and was refused it for having a different name. Removing the name test leaves the four real conditions untouched — this deletes a refusal, it does not add a check.

patches.why: CORRECTNESS, not plumbing — the only patch here that changes what a number MEANS, so it is declared loudly. toDouble accepted its fast path whenever the quotient was FINITE. Once the denominator passes ~1024 bits while the numerator does not, Number(d) is Infinity, finite/Infinity is 0, and Number.isFinite(0) is true: the scaling fallback was never reached and the function returned ZERO. Because toDouble reports enclosure WIDTHS, a certified bracket read as width zero, i.e. infinitely precise. Found 2026-08-31 when the Erdos #290 squeeze reached horizon l = 309 and the report page crashed on log10(0) — an accident of a log axis, not a gate. The test is now on the heights, before any conversion. THE SAME DEFECT IS PRESENT UPSTREAM in sin-mfg at research/challenges/erdos290/rational.js and in this repo's own instruments/interval/rational.js; the latter is fixed identically and carries red control X6 in instruments/interval/tests/test-interval.js. sin-mfg is READ-ONLY and was NOT touched — reported, not repaired, per CLAUDE.md.

patches.why: CORRECTNESS, in dated edits declared here on 2026-11-16 (the 2026-10-09 ones had been made and never declared, so PROVENANCE.json still named the lift-time bytes, patched false). 2026-10-09 (the code read of Phase 0): the domain enforced — every arithmetic operation refuses a malformed operand (not a pair of numbers, NaN, lo > hi) or an indeterminate result (0·∞, ∞−∞) by throw, through wf/out, and wf is exported; pow refuses an exponent at or beyond 2^31, where its 32-bit `e & 1` / `e >>= 1` returned [1,1]. 2026-11-16, two approved fixes in one commit: contains(a, x) requires a finite x — ±∞ was a member of any interval with that infinite end, the two ITF1788 violations isMember ∓infinity [entire] of certs/kernel-itf1788.json; and the padded platform cos/sin helper (trigAbsPad, encloseCos, encloseSin: Math.cos/Math.sin, which ECMAScript gives no accuracy bound, widened by a derived pad under an unwritten argument-error contract) is retired, its six callers moved to transcendental.js's proved series sin/cos. Every record that pinned the kernel's digest was re-derived by the new bytes each time (certs/erratum-2026-10-09.json; the 2026-11-16 re-derivation, the return-level atlas after it), except the Petrobras submissions, frozen as submitted and pinning the kernel of their dates (tools/pinned-at.js).

SOUNDNESS (2026-10-21, lane A of the method-paper review; declared here on 2026-11-16, never declared before): the remainders of the exp, log, sin and cos series are interval products with the upper end taken, every operation outward; before, they were computed round-to-nearest with one nextUp, sound only by the margin below the ulp of the sum.

CORRECTNESS (2026-10-09 code read; declared here on 2026-11-16, never declared before): the radii polynomial refuses a Y0 or Z2 that is negative, NaN or infinite — the old test !(Z2 > 0) sent a negative Z2 and a NaN into the linear branch and certified them — and the linear branch (Z2 = 0) proves p(r) < 0 as an interval inequality before it says ok, as the other branch always did.

CORRECTNESS (2026-10-09 code read; declared here on 2026-11-16, never declared before): the Certificate class refuses a falsifier list holding an empty string, and evidence for a PROVED verdict that is not a finite number, an interval of finite numbers, a BigInt, a non-empty string or a boolean ({k: undefined} passed and then serialised as the {} the constructor refuses).

the checks for the 2026-10-09 kernel edits (declared here on 2026-11-16, never declared before): S4 was vacuous — f.map(I.iv) is the Array.map arity trap, iv(x, index) built [0.5, 0] boxes — and now builds thin boxes; R3b–R3e refuse a negative or NaN Z2 and a negative Y0, and require the linear branch's interval proof.

the checks for the kernel's dated edits (declared here on 2026-11-16; the 2026-10-09 ones had never been declared). 2026-10-09: X7 pow refuses exponents at and beyond 2^31, X8 NaN, inverted and 0·∞ operands refused while infinite endpoints stay sound bounds. 2026-11-16: membership refuses ±∞ and NaN even in [−∞, +∞], with X5 the old membership test as its red control (X5 was the remembered ±1e-15 trig pad); the padded-helper tests are removed — trigAbsPad against 2·ε·|ang|, ±1e-15 against the pad, and encloseCos(x) ∋ Math.cos(x), a tautology — and the helper's retirement is checked.
